headline: Iambic Therapeutics, an Nvidia-backed company that uses AI to find cancer drugs, has launched a US share sale aiming to raise up to $159 million.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a mid-sized biotech listing, useful as a gauge of IPO appetite.
importance_line: What changed is that an AI drug company is testing public investors' appetite while other listings are delayed, which matters to investors and, if its drug candidates work, to patients with solid tumours, then to Iambic and its partners AbbVie and Takeda, and the doubt is that its value depends on unproven drugs in its pipeline more than on the AI itself.
summary: Reuters reports that Iambic is offering about 9.38 million shares at $15 to $17 each on the Nasdaq under the symbol IAM, a sale that would value it at up to $805.8 million according to a regulatory filing, with ARK Investment Management and Duquesne Family Office signalling interest in $60 million of shares. Reuters notes that AI drug discovery is one of the few areas still drawing investor interest in an IPO market hit by delays, while an analyst calls Iambic "a clinical-stage biotech company with an AI-enhanced drug discovery platform, rather than a pure AI play".
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); text read on SRN News and AOL.ca copies of the Reuters story.
